F01.note: Bahamut towers nicely over the girls' backs on the phone, but they pile up behind their HP cards and the bottom third below the three commands is dead space.

F02.note: Tidus's glowing sword leads the eye from behind him, but Seymour sits small and far off and Kimahri is lost behind Tidus.

F03.note: The gilded proscenium and curtains are a bold look, but they shrink Gagazet into a puppet stage and eat a fifth of the screen.

F04.note: Seymour looms big on the left while my party is a tiny line on the far right; the sides feel swapped and the heroes are an afterthought.

F05.note: Persona-style triptych is slick trailer material, but the actual fight is squeezed into the middle panel and the HUD sits on top of the art.

F06.note: Over Yuna's shoulder with the HUD tucked into cinema bands: tidy and deep, though Paine stands inside Bahamut's silhouette and the bands cost scale.

F07.note: The three girls lined up facing Bahamut down the lamp-lit corridor: balanced, clear and a little safe.

F08.note: Bahamut alone with the girls reduced to portrait cards; a great dragon, but where is my party?

F09.note: Classic three-quarter line-up with the HUD in bands reads perfectly, but the letterbox shrinks the mountain and it feels like watching on a TV.

F10.note: Low over-the-shoulder with Seymour looming over the party is exactly the FFX command feeling, though Kimahri vanishes behind Tidus.

F11.note: The whole screen mirrored, menu right and party facing left, looks fine but feels like FFX played in a mirror.

F12.note: Bahamut fills the frame and dwarfs a tiny huddle of girls pasted in front of his tail; big event, weak heroes.

F13.note: Board-game tokens on a map: no fight, no Gagazet, no event.

F14.note: Gorgeous rim-lit reverse shot, but it is an enemy-turn camera: I choose my command staring at Seymour's back with my party as specks.

F15.note: The three girls' backs in the foreground with Bahamut rearing up behind them; the most premium, most boss-event frame in the whole set.

F16.note: Solid three-quarter FFX staging with soft bokeh; the menu slab sits on Tidus's legs and sword.

F17.note: The girls bunch up in the middle with Paine hidden and Bahamut shrunk behind them; the heavy bokeh cannot save the clutter.

F18.note: Seymour towering over the party's backs with all three at least partly visible: very FFX, a little crowded in the middle.

F19.note: Same line-up as the plain three-quarter corridor shot with big bokeh orbs: slightly more mood, slightly more lens dust.

F20.note: Behind Tidus with Kimahri and Yuna fanned out and Seymour framed between them; this looks and reads like FFX's own command camera.

F21.note: Bahamut big and centred with the girls leading the eye into him; strong, though Yuna, whose turn it is, is cropped into the corner.

F22.note: Near-twin of the big-Bahamut shoulder shot, with the wing pushed under the menu and Paine pressed against the dragon.

F23.note: Best phone layout: Seymour big over the party's backs, turn order across the top, six commands in a tidy grid.

F24.note: Pretty poster with no HUD, but the girls face me with Bahamut behind them like it is their summon; key art, not a fight.

F25.note: Yuna's giant face owns half the screen with the boss bar sitting on her hair; a dating-sim frame, not a battle.

F26.note: Moody rim-lit Bahamut silhouette, but he is cropped by the edge and buried under the menu while the girls are specks.

F27.note: FFX-2's pop swagger suits comic panels better than FFX does, but the HUD piles onto the Bahamut panel and Rikku is sliced in half by a border.

F28.note: The fanned over-the-shoulder shot with the HUD pushed into bands: the cleanest read in the set, but it loses the full-bleed drama.

F29.note: Beautiful key art, but with no HUD and the party posing at me with their backs to Seymour it is a box cover, not a battle.

F30.note: Near-twin of the bokeh three-quarter shot with a moon instead of orbs: readable and familiar, but not an event.

F31.note: Dragon Quest first-person framing: Seymour looks great, but my party exists only as HUD cards.

F32.note: Flat side-on staging with tiny girls at left and Bahamut at right half under the menu: readable but lifeless.

F33.note: Tight over-the-shoulder is dramatic, but Kimahri disappears and the HP panel lands on Yuna.

F34.note: A giant Tidus face parked permanently on the battle screen, with a smeared edge; a cut-in frozen into the layout.

F35.note: Mirrored shoulder shot with Bahamut on the left has nice depth, but the girls are jammed against the menu and HP panel.

F36.note: Old-school party-on-the-right side view, squeezed between Bahamut and the menu.

F37.note: Looking down on the arena turns the party into standees and leaves Seymour, my target, out of focus.

F38.note: Yuna turns to the camera instead of the dragon and Paine hides behind her; pretty, but the staging looks away from the fight.

F39.note: The theatre frame again: a diorama of the fight with Yuna small in a spotlight.

F40.note: High angle with the girls surrounding Bahamut and hard shadows exposing the cards; not how FFX-2 lines up a fight.

F41.note: Yuna's back big in the foreground and the other two squaring up to Bahamut: lovely depth, though Paine melts into the dragon.

F42.note: Flat side-on line-up with an empty floor and a tiny party: clear, but no event and no FFX camera.

F43.note: Worm's-eye colossus sells Seymour as a boss, but the party looks pasted onto his robe at his feet.

F44.note: Isometric tactics grid: a handsome floor, but the girls and Bahamut are miniatures on a board.

F45.note: Shoulder shot flipped to the right: the menu eats the Mortiorchis and the HP panel eats Tidus.

F46.note: Mirrored three-quarter with the girls on the right and a nicely lit corridor behind; solid, but the whole layout reads flipped.

S01.note: This is FFX's camera grammar: over the shoulder to choose, low three-quarter for the hit, reverse for the enemy, worm's-eye for the big move, hero angle for the win, cutting on action beats rather than menu presses (the party HP panel is missing from the command shot, though).

S02.note: Each submenu gets its own angle inside cinema bands; readable, but flicking through the menu will cut the camera on every press.

S03.note: The camera moves on every menu step and the flower reticle leaves Bahamut soft exactly when I am aiming at him; the item push-in is all Paine.

S04.note: A slow idle orbit is nice life, but the pillar wipe blacks out the whole screen and Bahamut comes back as a different, redder painting.

S05.note: Cutting behind Tidus for Attack and high for magic gives each command its own shot, but the camera changes on every menu press.

S06.note: Following each girl's turn with a Persona-style cut-in is flashy once, but in FFX-2's quick ATB a cut-in every turn would wear thin fast.

S07.note: Smooth crane and dolly moves feel expensive, but it racks the target soft exactly when I am choosing it.

S08.note: The high three-girls-from-behind skill shot is lovely; the close item shot is a wall of Paine's hair, and it moves on every menu press.

S09.note: A whole FFX round from behind each actor with Seymour's attacks craned high feels right; the Kimahri name cut-in is fun but not FFX and would tire every turn.

S10.note: Whip pans on every menu press: a smear of blur each time I open a list, tiring within one fight.

S11.note: Locked camera: perfectly readable and never tiring, but the Bahamut fight never becomes an event.

S12.note: Locked FFX camera: clean and dependable but lifeless; I remember the real game's camera drifting while you choose.

S13.note: An FFX-2 turn played as an event: over Paine's shoulder, side-on hit, reverse for Bahamut, a worm's-eye Mega Flare wind-up and a proper victory pose.

S14.note: Whip pans with Bahamut's hit riding the blur: I lose the dragon, the damage and my place in the menu.

top5.reason: The FFX command camera: behind the active character, the party fanned so all three read, Seymour framed as the destination, HUD in FFX's corners (commands left, HP bottom right, turn order top right).
The same idea for FFX-2 at its most premium: big backs, a rearing Bahamut, warm bokeh; screenshot-worthy and unmistakably a boss event.
Seymour towering over the party's backs; the most boss-event FFX frame that still keeps the whole party readable.
Lower and closer than F18 so Seymour dominates even more; the drama pick, at the cost of Kimahri hiding behind Tidus.

Puts the active character, Yuna, big in the foreground with the other two squaring up to Bahamut; the best whose-turn-is-it shot for FFX-2 (F28 and F23 score as well but are the banded and phone versions of the same idea).

bottom3.reason: Tokens on a map: it throws away the paintings, the arena and every bit of FFX feel.
The overhead angle turns the painted cards into standees and blurs Seymour, the one thing I need to see sharply.
A tactics-game board with miniature figures; the boss and the heroes lose all their presence.

topSequences.reason: FFX's own grammar; the cuts land on action beats (hit, enemy turn, big move, win) and never on menu browsing, so it stays exciting without tiring.
The FFX-2 twin of S01; Mega Flare from a worm's-eye and a real victory pose make the fight an event.
Hands the camera to whoever's turn it is, from behind, across a full round, which is how FFX does it; drop the per-turn name cut-in and it is a keeper.

wholeGame: F20 for the FFX chapters and F15 for the FFX-2 chapters. The command camera sits behind the party, so I see my characters' backs squaring up to a boss that owns the middle of the frame. That is how both games hand you a turn, the back paintings make the cards feel like bodies standing in the arena, and the HUD stays at the edges instead of on the art. Then let S01 (and its FFX-2 twin S13) drive the camera once I confirm: low three-quarter for the hit, reverse for the enemy turn, worm's-eye for the big attack, a low hero angle for the win, cutting on action beats, never on menu presses, and never whip-panning. Keep the three-quarter line-ups (F07, F16) as the wide establishing shot, and leave the tokens, overhead boards, giant faces and poster poses out of play.
